solution: \(y=\cos(x+y)\). Differentiate implicitly: \(y'=-\sin(x+y)(1+y') \Rightarrow y'=\dfrac{-\sin(x+y)}{1+\sin(x+y)}\). The tangent is parallel to \(x+2y=0\) (slope \(-\tfrac12\)), so \(\dfrac{-\sin(x+y)}{1+\sin(x+y)}=-\tfrac12 \Rightarrow 2\sin(x+y)=1+\sin(x+y) \Rightarrow \sin(x+y)=1 \Rightarrow x+y=\tfrac{\pi}{2}\). Then \(y=\cos\tfrac{\pi}{2}=0\), so \(x=\tfrac{\pi}{2}\) and the point is \(\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2},0\right)\). Tangent: \(y-0=-\tfrac12\left(x-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \Rightarrow 2x+4y-\pi=0\). Hence option B.
